items.title: em.transactional() resolves although PostgreSQL rolled the transaction back (caught error, then COMMIT)
items.body:
A statement fails inside a transaction on PostgreSQL, and the application catches the error and returns normally. MikroORM then sends `COMMIT`.

PostgreSQL answers that `COMMIT` with the command tag `ROLLBACK`. It does not raise another error. `pg` resolves the query, and `result.command` is `ROLLBACK`. `em.transactional()` resolves with the callback's return value.

The transaction API resolves successfully even though PostgreSQL rolled back every write.

The transactions docs advise rethrowing a caught exception, or rolling back. That is sound application advice. It does not change what this `COMMIT` already answered. The reply is `ROLLBACK`, and that reply is discarded before the API resolves.

If any later statement is sent, it fails with `25P02` and the error is loud. The silent case is the one where the caught error is the last thing that happens before commit.

The same sequence on bare Kysely, with no MikroORM, has the same outcome. `commit().execute()` resolves, and `db.transaction().execute()` returns the callback's value. The inserted row is absent. `pg`'s command tag for that `COMMIT` is `ROLLBACK`. This is Kysely 0.29.6 and 0.29.7. The tag is dropped inside Kysely: `PostgresConnection.executeQuery()` reads `command` off the `pg` result and returns only `{ numAffectedRows, rows }`. `PostgresDriver.commitTransaction()` ignores the result. MikroORM's `AbstractSqlConnection.commit()` awaits `ctx.commit().execute()` and treats resolution as success. In the 7.2.5 source, `afterTransactionCommit` is dispatched after that await. This run did not record the subscriber.

## Reproduction

`@mikro-orm/postgresql@7.2.5`, `pg@8.23.1`, a scratch database. This is one transaction. Nothing is nested.

```js
// DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres node repro.mjs
import { MikroORM, defineEntity, p } from '@mikro-orm/postgresql'

const User = defineEntity({ name: 'M3User', properties: { id: p.integer().primary().autoincrement(), email: p.string().unique() } })
const Audit = defineEntity({ name: 'M3Audit', properties: { id: p.integer().primary().autoincrement(), action: p.string() } })

const orm = await MikroORM.init({
  clientUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
  entities: [User, Audit],
  ensureDatabase: false,
})
await orm.schema.refresh()
await orm.em.fork().insert(User, { email: 'taken@example.com' })

const result = await orm.em.fork().transactional(async (em) => {
  em.create(Audit, { action: 'signup-attempt' })
  await em.flush()
  try {
    em.create(User, { email: 'taken@example.com' })
    await em.flush()
  } catch (e) {
    console.log('caught', e.constructor.name)
  }
  return 'committed'
}).then((v) => v, (e) => `rejected: ${e.constructor.name}`)

console.log('em.transactional():', result)
console.log('audit rows:', await orm.em.fork().count(Audit))
await orm.close()
```

Observed 2026-10-18, PostgreSQL 18.6, Node 24.14.1. The statements `pg` recorded, in order: `begin`, the audit `insert`, the user `insert` (`23505`), `commit` with command tag `ROLLBACK`. No `savepoint`.

```text
caught UniqueConstraintViolationException
em.transactional(): committed
audit rows: 0
```

A joined `em.transactional(..., { propagation: REQUIRED })` does the same. Its trace is also `begin`, two inserts, `commit` / `ROLLBACK`. There is no `savepoint`. The outer call resolves, and the outer row is absent.

`pg` alone:

```js
const res = await client.query('commit') // after a failed statement in the same transaction
console.log(res.command) // ROLLBACK
```

Bare Kysely, `startTransaction()` then `commit().execute()`, and `db.transaction().execute()` with the error caught inside the callback: both resolve, the row is absent, and the `COMMIT` command tag is `ROLLBACK`. Same on 0.29.6 and 0.29.7.

## Expected behavior

When PostgreSQL answers `COMMIT` with `ROLLBACK`, the transaction API should reject.

The direct check is the command tag. It is the outcome of this statement. It does not require remembering every earlier error, and it does not add a round trip. The obstacle is that the tag does not leave Kysely.

Tracking an aborted flag can also work, and it is more than a boolean. Savepoints nest. A `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` that succeeds restores the error state only as far as that savepoint. Some errors end the connection instead. I would not call that path free of happy-path cost without spelling out those cases.

A `select 1` in `beforeTransactionCommit` is a workaround. In an aborted transaction it fails with `25P02`, so the commit is not silent. It costs a round trip, and the probe does not prove that the `COMMIT` which follows will succeed.

## Suggested regression tests

1. One `em.transactional()` callback inserts a row, catches a unique violation, and returns. The call rejects, and the row is absent.
2. The same through `em.begin()` and `em.commit()`. `em.commit()` rejects.
3. No false positive. A `NESTED` callback inserts a row and throws. Its savepoint rolls back. The outer callback inserts a different row and returns. The outer call resolves, the outer row is present, and the inner row is absent. Observed today: that outer `COMMIT` has command tag `COMMIT`.

If the fix is the command tag, a lower-level test should see `ROLLBACK` from `COMMIT` and fail the commit.

## Related

**#8458** (PR #8462) is a failed `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` that is swallowed, so the inner writes can commit with the outer transaction. Different trigger. Its note that a later statement then fails with `25P02` is the loud case. This issue is the case where nothing follows the caught error, so `COMMIT` itself does not fail.

## Versions

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Driver | `@mikro-orm/postgresql` |
| MikroORM version | 7.2.5 (`core`, `postgresql`, `sql`). Still the latest release on 2026-10-18. The postgresql package depends on `kysely@0.29.6`. |
| Also run | bare `kysely` 0.29.6 and 0.29.7, `pg` 8.23.1 |
| Node.js version | v24.14.1 |
| Operating system | macOS (Darwin 25.6, arm64); PostgreSQL 18.6 (`postgres:18`) |
